To begin our work on Middos, we first must delve into understanding what Middos are actually. 
Our biggest mistake is that we think a middeh is a certain hydraulic pressure in your body, in your stomach somewhere, You have some pressure to do chesed. You call that the koiches ha’nefesh. And this pressure is pushing you to make chesed. Or when you have Middas Ha’Emes, you have an inner affinity or inner drive for truth. 
So whatever Midda you want, when you have bad Middos or Taivas, the same thing, you have some stomach problems. That means you get excited or hot or whatever it is in your body for something, food or for other things, we'll speak about that. And that's what Taivas are. 
I think the whole thing is a mistake. Middos are not like this. They are not pressures in your body. Middos are something much deeper. Middos are, I don't have an English word for that. I said in Hebrew. Also in Hebrew there is a difference between regesh and hergesh. Middos are hergeshim in a mehalech of seichel. You have a concept and the hergesh of that concept, that's the Midda. But it's always a concept going on inside. A Midda is not just some hargoshe, some feeling. A Midda is always a hergesh in a concept. 
For example, R’ Yisroel says that ga'ive is a hergish in two things; שבח עצמו וחסרון זולתו. You have a whole mehalech that you want to hear your own ma’alos. And you have a whole mehalech that you want to see bad things in other people. And there you have a hergish. 
That means this person will be able to enumerate his own chisrones - his shortcomings - one by one. He'll say, I'm choser in this, I'm lacking in that, I'm wrong in this, I'm mistaken in that. But he has no hergish for it. It doesn't create any hergish, it's a pure hakoreh. 
That is a Baal Gai’veh. Because the Baal ga'ive will know that he has chishorinus. And he even doesn't make a mistake. He will know it. And he'll tell you about that. He'll speak it out. But he has no hergish. It's a hakoreh without hergish. 
That's not the midde. The midde is that there is a mehalech. The mehalech of אהבת שבח עצמו. And the mehalech of אהבת חסרון זולתו. And by that you have a hergish in it. You feel it. That was called Abbas. You feel that. That's what the midde is. And midde always, always has a concept inside. Middes are not mere pressures or excitements or whatever it is. It's always a concept inside. 
That is the reason I never wanted to work on Tayves A'chilleh personally. I'm willing to go on a diet, but not to actually work on Tayves A'chilleh because I'm afraid of this gehenem which is inside Tayves A'chilleh. Because Tayves A'chilleh is not about the sweetness of the ice cream or the amazing taste of a steak. That's your mistake. You think that's what Tayves A'chilleh is about. 
No, it's not. Tayves A'chilleh is something very deep and very, very dangerous; you want to live without the Borei Olam. You don't want to have Hakoras HaTov. You want to be self-sufficient. You are having a merida against the Borei Olam. You don't think about your chaverim and you don't think about anyone else. You don't have a Hakoras HaTov to any human being. You simply want to live with your own reality. That's it. 
And that's what Tayves A'chilleh is a hergish in that. It's not, now you make a mistake, you think, I have enjoyment from the food. Yeah. Even when you work on Tayves A'chilleh, you still have to have hanoeh. Otherwise your brocheh is a brocheh le’vatoleh; to make a brocheh you need hanoeh. Because hanoeh is kodesh kodoshim. Hanoeh is not Tayves A'chilleh, Tayves A'chilleh is something else. Tayves A'chilleh is a hergish in a very rotten deep-rooted concept.

.So, for the opener, think about writing down things, such as:

.If you’re applying for multiple courses, think about how your skills, academic interests, and the way you think are relevant to all the courses you’ve chosen. Don’t begin with the overkill opening
.Try not to overthink the opening sentence. You need to engage the reader with your relevant thoughts and ideas, but not go overboard.
.Tutors said: ‘The opening is your chance to introduce yourself, to explain your motivation for studying the course and to demonstrate your understanding of it. The best personal statements get to the point quickly. Go straight in. What excites you about the course and why do you want to learn about it more?’
.Be succinct and draw the reader in, but not with a gimmick. This isn’t the X Factor.

2. Write about why you want to study that course
.Think about why you want to study the course and how you can demonstrate this in your written statement:
.’Your interest in the course is the biggest thing. Start with a short sentence that captures the reason why you’re interested in studying the area you’re applying for and that communicates your enthusiasm for it. Don’t waffle or say you want to study something just because it’s interesting. Explain what you find interesting about it.’
.It’s much better to engage us with something interesting, relevant, specific and current in your opening line… Start with what’s inspiring you now, not what inspired you when you were six.
3. Avoid cliches
.Try to avoid cliches and the most obvious opening sentences so you stand out from the very first line. UCAS publishes a list of common opening lines each year. Here are just some overused phrases to avoid using in your personal statement:
From a young age…
For as long as I can remember…
I am applying for this course because…
I have always been interested in…
Throughout my life I have always enjoyed…
And try not to use quotes. Quotations are top of the list of admissions tutors’ pet hates.

.’Concentrate on the main content of your statement and write the introduction last. I think the opening line is the hardest one to write, so I often say leave it until the end and just try and get something down on paper.’
.It may be easier to get on with writing the main content of your statement and coming back to the introduction afterwards –that way you will also know what you’re introducing.
.I often advise applicants to start with paragraph two, where you get into why you want to study the course. That’s what we’re really interested in.

.Why will you be great?

.Your personal skills and achievements

.Next, you’ll need to write about your personal skills and achievements. Universities like to know the abilities you have that’ll help you on the course, or generally with life at university.
.Don’t forget to include evidence to back up why you’re so excited about the course(s) you’ve chosen.
.Be bold and talk about the achievements you’re proud of.
.Include positions of responsibility you hold, or have held, both in and out of school.
.What are the things that make you interesting, special, or unique?

.You want to leave the admissions tutor reading your personal statement with a strong lasting impression – one that will leave them no choice but to make you an offer (or invite you to an interview).
.There are several ways you can do this.
.HE Careers Adviser Liz says:
.A good ending can link back to what you claim at the beginning or be a short summary as to what you’re looking forward to at university, new challenges etc… or even your commitment as to why you would be an ideal candidate (without bragging).
.Don’t waffle
.Think about what you’re writing in this critical spot – what’s your reason for including it here? Keep the ending of your personal statement short, concise and to the point.
.Avoid famous quotes
.Like the start of your personal statement, try to avoid cliches, quotes or asking rhetorical questions you’re not going to answer.
.Make yourself stand out
.Careers expert Alan Bullock says: 'Give them one more little insight into your ideas, interests, or skills, or be specific about something you personally want to achieve from the course or from your wider university experience.’
.Keep notes as you write
.Inspiration can strike when you least expect, especially while you’re writing the main section of your statement. Note any thoughts down straightaway so you can come back to them when you’re ready.
.How to end your personal statement: What to write
.A key academic skill at degree level is being able to form a structured written argument, including a conclusion that summarises the key points.
.As Liverpool student Joseph says:
.You don’t want a conclusion in the same way as you would for an essay, as that’s just taking away from your word count. Don’t draw it out.’
.In other words, keep it to the point and punchy.
.There’s no set way to end your statement. Instead, think about the following and how it might help you to stand out:
.Tie it back to what you’ve written earlier
.Revisit the key points you’ve already spoken about in the main body of your personal statement and emphasise them again in your conclusion. This could be reiterating key skills, interests, and experiences you’ve already touched on, giving them one last chance to hit home (but don’t just regurgitate what you’ve already said).
.Talk about the future
.Looking to the future is an optimistic way to finish. It shows you’re goal-oriented, and you’ve carefully thought about how this course fits into your plans. You don’t need to have the next ten years mapped out, but if you’ve a broad sense of your career path – or any related life ambitions you want to fill – it’s worth mentioning them here, as well as how this course will help you achieve those.
.Learn more about career prospects for your subject (and more) in our subject guides.
.Think about your university experience
.You could conclude by talking more generally about what you want to get from your overall university experience. For instance:
.Would you like to build your confidence meeting people from a variety of backgrounds?
.Are you hoping to engage with a local community through a mutual passion or vocation?
.Also, talk about how you will be an asset to a university.
.Remember, all of your UCAS choices will see your personal statement, so it may be best to keep it general, rather than being specific about one university.

What makes a resume great can be subjective, but below are some common
characteristics associated with the ‘great’ resumes:

Provide a DETAILED discussion of your responsibilities, duties and accomplishments. Be honest but don’t be humble. Give SUBSTANTIVE explanations of your achievements; Led and supervised squad of 10 rifleman in all daily tasks and operations, effectively managed program X to Y & Z results, mentored XX employees, sailors, etc, managed $XXX,XXX worth of equipment, budget or resources. Some thoughts: What did you do that supported your command or company? How did you contribute to the overall operation or mission? How did your subordinates benefit from your leadership, IE; development, retention, promotion numbers,
awards received, etc. NO FLUFF OR BUZZ WORDS! No “results driven”, “detail oriented” or “outside the box” comments. They may sound impressive but trust that recruiters and hiring managers see it on hundreds of resumes. Honestly, the only thing generic fluff & buzz words say about your history and performance is that you don’t have anything else to say. Avoid that perception and stick with quantifiable examples.
Again, be honest but don’t be humble and sell yourself as being able to do a job by demonstrating HOW you’ve done It (or related work) previously! 

**Concise and appropriate language**
-Sufficient detail to convey experiences
- Eliminate ‘fluff’ language or unnecessary words, and replace with
more powerful action words
- Example: “The team’s project was centered around increasing the revenue of
Business unit A” “Collaborated with team to increase revenue of business unit
by 20%”
• Experiences are well-communicated and convey that you have the
skills for the job
- Explicitly explains what you did and what the results were
-Calls out instances of leadership, initiative, teamwork, etc.
• There are no holes

**Word Choice**
• Short, powerful sentences beginning with action verb
• Variety of word choice (don’t start with the same word more than twice)
• Avoid personal pronouns (I, me, my) – write in third person
• Use appropriate tense (if something happened in past, use the past tense)
• Avoid acronyms, contractions (e.g. don’t, can’t), abbreviations or slang

**Sufficient Detail**
Sell yourself because applicants you are competing against are doing the
same!
• Explain what you have done clearly enough, so that someone who has no
idea what your job entailed can understand it
- Having others read your resume is a good test
• Quantify and note results wherever possible
- Can significantly increases your credibility
- Example: “Increased membership and led fundraiser”
“Increased membership by 30% and led 10 peers in bake sale fundraiser to raise $4,000 for our organization” (then elaborate a bit more on what you did to achieve this

**Formatting**
Poor formatting will almost guarantee your resume does not get the
attention it deserves!
• Use bolding, italics, underlining and spacing appropriately to provide
structure and organization – but do not go overboard

Nobody really knows what caused there to be a size difference between macros and micros. One thing we know is that it didn’t always used to be like this. There were no over-sized plants and vegetation that destroyed houses with their roots and vines, there were no insects that could grow to the size of a compact car, and there were definitely no macro furries that delighted in hunted down and swallowing their smaller cousins whole. This, however, was all before the rise of the macros.

As you can imagine, there was a great deal of confusion when one day regular furries, animals, and plants rapidly began to grow to many times their original size whereas the anthropomorphic mammals remained at their normal sizes. At first, there seemed to be at least some form of cooperation between the two groups as they tried to repair the damage that had been done. However, the giants soon started to give up on the idea that the two groups could ever be considered equal. This was largely due to the fact that an average adult-sized micro was only about three inches tall when compared to one of the massive giants. Micros were crushed beneath the macro’s feet without a second glance (sometimes intentionally) as the giants trudged about their daily lives.

Some micros gathered together and fled to remote locations away from most of the dangers that they faced. This didn’t protect them from everything however. No matter where they went, there was always something big that had it’s eye on them. Even if there were no macrofurries around, micros found themselves being eaten alive by the animals that had grown on that day as well.

Several years passed after the rise of the macros, and for the micros, things only became worse. Macros on the other hand had used that time to build the beginnings of fully macro-sized towns and cities where they could live normal lives again.
Ash was an anthropomorphic pardinensis cheetah, a very rare species, he was a micro. He was slim and muscular with a long and thin tail and a short grey fur with darker spots, his short sleek fur was letting see the chiseled details of his muscles. He was also quite intelligent, but perhaps not as much as he thought to be. He despised the other micros who chose to live as far possible from the towering macros and their cities. He was living in their gigantic houses, hiding under their building seized pieces of furniture of in the holes in their walls.
But one day he was captured and sold to a macro.
When the box was finally opened and Ash was brought out, he was met with the sight of a towering anthro jaguar. The massively muscular jaguar grinned down at him, his sharp teeth glinting in the light.

“Well, well, well,” the jaguar said with a chuckle. “Looks like I won myself a tasty little snack.”

Ash shuddered in fear as the jaguar lifted him up, examining him closely. The jaguar smirked as he examined the body of the comparatively diminutive cheetah. “Fine, you seem to have endured the travel quite well. I bought that cage for you, I hope you will find it large enough. From the description on the auction site you’re a freshly caught wild micro. I assume you’re not used to restrained space, but you have to get used to it.” He chuckled and put Ash in the cage. He closed the door of the enclosure just after. “I can’t wait to have some fun with you, but it’s better to let you have some rest to chill out a bit.” Then the jaguar moved on his couch to watch TV, time to time he cast a glance at the cage and his tiny occupant from his seat. Some time later he moved to his bedroom to sleep for the night.

The jaguar came back at the end of the day. He brought several grocery sacks and put them in his kitchen. “I thought about eating you first, but you’re so tiny you would not even fill one tenth of my belly.” He said with a chuckle. Some time later he come back with a dinner TV for carnivores adapted to his enormous size. He reached in the cage for the cheetah. Ash tried to avoid to be grabbed and managed to stay out of the reach of the humongous jaguar paw like hand as he was holding his dinner TV with his other hand at the same time, but the giant managed to seize the cheetah diminutive body eventually. “Don’t make your difficult to get !” Said the jaguar with the same chuckle. He then moved to his couch and sat heavily, the couch creaking under the thousands of tons of his weight. He then put the cheetah on the rim of the tray of his dinner TV. “Several kinds of meat. Beef, chicken, fish, and caiman, my favorite !” He said. “You can take some, it’s not your appetite that will make a difference.” He switched his TV on and searched for something interesting with his remote while taking some bit of food time to time. “Ah, by the way, my name is Lance. But you have to call me Master.” He snickered. “Or, if you feel like being a good pet, Daddy.” He laughed.

One day, when Lance was engrossed in a particularly loud show on television, Ash seized his chance. As the jaguar laughed uproariously at the antics on the screen, he quietly slid out of his cage and onto the floor, careful to avoid any creaking or telltale sounds. Using his memory of the house layout and the cacophony of the TV, he stealthily made his way towards the window that he had observed Lance often leaving open.

Ash’s heart pounded as he reached the window, with each passing second a potential for Lance to notice him. With one final act of defiance against his captor, he climbed up the curtain and leapt out into the open air, finally free. As he made his way through the grass that seemed like a jungle, he knew that he had a long journey ahead of him. But no matter where life would take him in this dangerous world, he had now proven to himself that he could face it with courage and determination.

Unknown of Ash, Lance was well aware about his position, as by security the giant jaguar put a microchip and GPS device in the collar he put around the neck of his expensive micro anthro cheetah.
Lance followed the moving of his pet on his car sized smartphone as an app what giving him the position of Ash on a map. And some hours later the jaguar resounding steps come close of the hideout of Ash.
“Ash ? I know you’re here. Move out of your hiding place.” The giant waited some seconds. “You know it’s dangerous for you to be in the streets. Critters are big here, they will eat you. And there are other macros too, all of them won’t try to catch you to keep you as a pet. So come with me. You will be safe in my home. I won’t punish you very hard for this time.”
Ash’s heart sank as he heard Lance’s intimidating voice. He knew that there was no denying the giant’s presence, but he was determined to make a final attempt to escape. From his hiding place, he quickly formed a plan.

Taking advantage of the giant’s momentary distraction, he bolted from his hiding place, running as fast as his legs could carry him, away from Lance. The jaguar gave an annoyed grunt and pursued Ash, his massive strides closing the distance between them frighteningly quickly.

In the midst of their chase, Ash recalled a large sewer drain he had discovered earlier during his exploration. Deftly, the micro cheetah made a sudden turn, darting into the drain and disappearing from Lance’s sight.

The giant jaguar cursed under his breath, realizing that he couldn’t fit into the small space. He knelt down, attempting to reach into the drain with his massive paw, but Ash was too fast and had already scrambled further into the darkness.

Lance growled lowly, frustrated at losing his prized pet. But he was also impressed by the cunning and determination of the small creature. He briefly considered calling off the chase and letting Ash make his own way in this harsh world, but the investment in the micro cheetah and his curiosity about whether Ash’s resourcefulness could be put to better use got the better of him.

The giant jaguar decided his next move - he’d take a different tactic. Anticipating the path of the sewers, Lance hurried towards another exit, where he would attempt to recapture Ash quietly and seemingly without effort. In a strange sense, the thrilling game of cat-and-mouse was starting to become intriguing and even somewhat enjoyable to Lance.

A macro centipede was hiding in the sewer. It was easily four time longer than Ash and about the length of Lance’s forearm. The cheetah inadvertently knocked one of the long antennas of the invertebrate. The centipede became active and started to run after the cheetah. Ash, as a former wild micro before being captured, was used to cross the way of some macro critters, but the place where he lived before being sold to Lance was more in the north of the country in a cooler climate and insects were not as big even the macro ones. That centipede was looking like a monster for the cheetah and he ran with terror while the invertebrate was chasing him.
Ash burst out of the sewer and didn’t even noticed Lance waiting for him. The centipede hurtled out of the sewer pursuing his tiny prey.
Lance quickly realized the danger posed to his tiny prize and jumped into action. With an impressive display of strength and agility, he caught the large centipede just as it was about to sink its venomous pincers into the panicked cheetah. He crushed the giant invertebrate without hesitation, its many legs twitching one last time before going completely limp.
Ash, still in a state of panic, finally noticed Lance standing above him. The skyscraper jaguar had saved him, and though Ash was desperate to escape captivity, he couldn’t help but feel a strange, begrudging gratitude toward Lance.

The jaguar offered a massive paw to Ash, smirking. “Now do you see why I told you it’s a dangerous world out there? You can stay with me, and I can keep you safe from creatures like that. Or you can go back out there alone, and take your chances with the countless other predators lurking in the shadows.”

Ash hesitated, torn between his desire for freedom and his newfound understanding of the true dangers faced by someone in his situation. He glanced back at the sewer entrance, shuddering at the memory of the terrifying macro centipede.

Reluctantly, he climbed into Lance’s outstretched palm, knowing that, for the moment, his best chance at survival was to accept the giant’s “protection”. As they walked back to Lance’s home, Ash wondered if he could ever change the dynamic of their relationship, and perhaps one day regain his freedom without sacrificing his safety.
Lance washed Ash meticulously as his escapade made the micro ran through a sewer. And the giant checked the diminutive anthro feline body to see if he had been hurt. Then he put him back in his cage and took care to close the door of the enclosure.
Later in that same day, Lance gently seized Ash in his massive hand and moved to his couch. He had another of these enormous dinner TV for macro carnivores and he offered some bits of meat to Ash.
Ash was about to eat one of them when he noticed something different. Lance didn’t switch the TV on yet. He put the morsel on the rim of the gigantic tray and looked up at Lance. Recognition of the cost of an asset as operating expense over the useful life of that asset.

**Depreciation of Hardware Assets:**
- Associated with Fixed Assets such as Buildings, Equipment, Computer Hardware (e.g. Servers and Storage Devices)

**Amortization of Software Assets:**

- Typical Software has a useful life of 3-5 years
- Straight line method is used to amortize costs over the useful life of the software

TESTICULAR SWELLING
ASK THE FOLLOWING QUESTIONS:
1. Is there pain or tenderness of the testicle? The presence of pain or
tenderness should suggest torsion of the testicle, orchitis, epididymitis,
and a strangulated inguinal hernia.
2. Is the testicle retracted or does elevation of the testicle aggravate
the pain? These findings would suggest torsion of the testicle. An
absent cremasteric reflex should also suggest torsion.
3. Does the swelling transilluminate? If the swelling transilluminates,
the mass or swelling is most likely a hydrocele or spermatocele.
4. Is the swelling reducible? If the swelling is reducible, the mass is
probably an inguinal hernia or varicocele. A mass that does not reduce
could still be an incarcerated inguinal hernia.
DIAGNOSTIC WORKUP
A CBC, sedimentation rate, urinalysis, chemistry panel, and VDRL test
should be done routinely. If a tumor of the testicle is suspected, 24-hour
urine gonadotrophins and alpha-fetoprotein levels may be ordered. If there
is a urethral discharge, a smear and culture for gonorrhea and chlamydia
should be done. If a hernia is strongly suspected, a general surgeon should
be consulted. Testicular scans with technetium-99m and ultrasonography
will help distinguish torsion of the testicle from orchitis or epididymitis.
Scrotal ultrasound may also be useful in differentiating a hematoma,
abscess, or rupture from orchitis. It may also be helpful in evaluating
testicular tumors. A CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis may be necessary
to rule out metastasis.
The expense of some or all of these tests may be avoided by consulting
an urologist early in the diagnostic workup.

ASK THE FOLLOWING QUESTIONS:
1. Is there a positive drug or alcohol history? Alcohol, amitriptyline,
diuretics, and many other drugs may cause excessive thirst.
2. Is there fever? The presence of fever would make one suspect an
infectious disease (see page 198).
3. Is there pallor or shock? Pallor or shock should make one think of
gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding, ruptured ectopic pregnancy, trauma,
and other disorders associated with anemia or shock.
4. Is there significant polyuria? Polyuria that is either significant or
massive would suggest diabetes insipidus, diabetes mellitus, or
thyrotoxicosis. Mild or insignificant polyuria may be because of
hypercalcemia, hyperparathyroidism, and excessive salt intake.
DIAGNOSTIC WORKUP
Routine tests include a CBC, sedimentation rate, urinalysis, chemistry
panel, thyroid panel, glucose tolerance test, blood alcohol level, and 24hour urine collection for sodium, potassium, and calcium. If pituitary
diabetes insipidus is suspected, a CT scan of the brain, the Hickey–Hare
test, and a vasopressin (Pitressin) injection test may need to be done. If
hyperparathyroidism is suspected, a serum PTH assay and x-ray of the
skull and long bones may be done. A consultation with an endocrinologist
may be necessary.

 THROMBOCYTOPENIA
ASK THE FOLLOWING QUESTIONS:
1. What is the WBC count? Thrombocytopenia with a high white count
suggests leukemia or myeloid metaplasia. Thrombocytopenia with a
normal white count suggests idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura or
drug reaction. Thrombocytopenia with a low white count suggests
lupus erythematosus, aplastic anemia, myelofibrosis, drugs,
myelophthisic anemia, or pernicious anemia.
2. What is the ANA? A positive ANA in the face of thrombocytopenia
and a low white count suggests lupus erythematosus.
DIAGNOSTIC WORKUP
The diagnostic workup should include a CBC, blood smear, sedimentation
rate, urinalysis, serum B12, chemistry panel, ANA, serum haptoglobins,
red cell survival, liver spleen scan, CT scan of the abdomen, and a
hematology consult for bone marrow study.

 THYROID ENLARGEMENT
ASK THE FOLLOWING QUESTIONS:
1. Is it focal or diffuse? Focal masses in the thyroid, include
thyroglossal cyst, toxic adenoma, colloid cyst, Riedel’s struma,
nontoxic adenoma, and malignancies.
2. Is there movement with protrusion of the tongue? This is a typical
finding in cases of thyroglossal cyst.
3. If focal, are there signs of thyrotoxicosis? The presence of

Routine tests include a CBC, sedimentation rate, urinalysis, thyroid profile

endocrinologist or general surgeon should be consulted to assist in the
interpretation. If the scan indicates a cold nodule, ultrasonography may be
done to determine whether the nodule is cystic or solid. If it is cystic,
generally it can be aspirated and followed. If it is solid, a CT scan or an
MRI is indicated before a biopsy or aspiration and biopsy are undertaken.
If there are malignant cells or at least suspicious cells for malignancy,
surgery should be done. If the scan reveals a hot nodule and there is
clinical and laboratory evidence of thyrotoxicosis, the patient should be

1. Is it subjective or objective? Objective tinnitus is unusual, but it may

middle or inner ear.

Pain in the tongue is rarely an isolated symptom. There is usually a focal
or diffuse inflammation of the tongue or an ulcerating lesion. Diffuse
inflammation is found in antibiotic glossitis, glossitis of avitaminosis

trauma, such as the bitten tongue or burned tongue (hot pizza, etc.), or
injury from a sharp tooth or jagged dental plate. Other painful focal lesions

ulcers. When the tongue is completely normal, trigeminal neuralgia,
polymyositis, trichinosis, and calculus of the submaxillary gland should be
considered.

Most lesions will respond to conservative treatment and time. In patients

dentist or oral surgeon.

Ulcerations of the tongue are most commonly because of aphthous
stomatitis (canker sore), but they may appear in various stages of syphilis,

others. To differentiate the other causes, a smear and culture and,
ultimately, a biopsy must be done. Most physicians will find referral to a

As physicians, we often neglect inspection of the teeth. We seem to expect

become misaligned. In dental ectodermal dysplasia, the teeth may be
partially or completely absent, and, at times, there is no evidence of
enamel formation. The dark blue line positioned where the gums meet the

You are asked to see a 46-year-old white female because of increasing

outstretched hands, which is sometimes described as tension tremor,

findings. A tremor with long tract findings, such as hyperactive
reflexes or Babinski’s sign, would suggest multiple sclerosis, whereas
a fairly symmetrical tremor with no long tract signs or other
neurologic findings would suggest a familial or senile tremor. A
tremor with mental deterioration would suggest Wilson’s disease.

tachycardia and an enlarged thyroid, one should consider
hyperthyroidism. However, simply tachycardia alone might indicate

Certainly, a thyroid profile should be done on all cases that present with a

cerebellar tumor is suspected, a CT scan or an MRI of the brain should be
done. When there is doubt as to whether the tremor is a resting or active
tremor, an EMG may be done to separate the two. Most patients presenting
with a mild intention tremor that is symmetrical and not associated with
other neurologic findings will probably have familial or senile tremor, and
the response to beta-blockers can be determined.

True trismus or lockjaw is found in tetanus, rabies, and trichinosis. In
strychnine poisoning, it is a late development, as the twitchings and
convulsions are well established before it appears. Intermittent trismus

impacted wisdom teeth, temporomandibular joint syndrome, scleroderma,
and malingering or hysteria. The diagnostic workup will be obvious in
cases of true trismus. Cases not associated with a systemic disease should
have an EEG and x-ray of the teeth and temporomandibular joints. A
referral to a dental specialist is often in order.

because recently, DNA probe testing, nucleic acid amplification and rapid
antigen testing of the urine have become available for gonorrhea and
chlamydia. A swab of the discharge can be utilized for the same testing. If
there are joint pains or uveitis, look for Reiter’s syndrome. Other
etiologies for nongonococcal urethritis are Ureaplasma genitalium and
Trichomonas vaginalis. Alert the laboratory, in advance, if these
organisms are suspected because they may require special culture media
for isolation. A prostate examination should always be done in males, as
acute and chronic prostatitis are common causes of urethral discharge. In
teenagers, a urethral discharge may develop from prolonged abstinence or
excessive masturbation. Rarer causes of urethral discharge are syphilis,
tuberculosis, foreign body, and herpes. Carcinoma of the urethra is
extremely rare. Anyone with a urethral discharge needs a VDRL test and
HIV antibody titer. Sexual partners should be tested as well.

633

 URINE COLOR CHANGES
Red urine may be because of hematuria (page 238), hemoglobinuria
(hemolytic anemia), myoglobinuria (muscle trauma, myocardial
infarction), and coproporphyria or uroporphyria (porphyria).
Phenazopyridine hydrochloride (Pyridium) also colors the urine red or
orange. Ingestion of large amounts of beets will also color the urine red.
Brown urine is usually because of hepatitis or obstructive jaundice, but
myoglobin and melanuria may also color the urine brown. Black urine is
found in malignant melanoma. Porphyrins may also color the urine black.
In alkaptonuria, the urine turns black on standing. Green or blue urine may
be found in patients taking methylene blue, indigo carmine, or indigo blue.
Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection may also turn urine green. The key to
the diagnostic workup is to send the urine to the laboratory for complete
analysis and culture. Most of the conditions listed above will have another
symptom that will offer additional keys to the diagnostic workup using
these pages.

634

 VAGINAL BLEEDING
ASK THE FOLLOWING QUESTIONS:
1. Is the vaginal examination normal? Cervical, endometrial, and
ovarian carcinomas are the most important possibilities to rule out.
Chronic cervicitis or vaginal trauma are just a few of the other
conditions to consider.
2. Is the pregnancy test positive? This test should always be done in
cases of vaginal bleeding. A positive test suggests threatened abortion,
ectopic pregnancy, or missed abortion among other conditions.
3. Is there a history of use of oral contraceptives or other
contraceptive devices? These most certainly may cause dysfunctional
uterine bleeding.
4. Is there pale conjunctiva or poor nutrition? Consider iron
deficiency anemia or anemia of other causes.
5. Is there tremor, tachycardia, or nonpitting edema? If so, a thyroid
disorder may be the cause.
Negative answers to all these questions prompt an investigation for
blood dyscrasias and collagen disease, but menopause and dysfunctional
uterine bleeding may be the cause.
DIAGNOSTIC WORKUP
A pregnancy test is a must in women of child-bearing age even if the
pelvic examination is normal. A pelvic ultrasound examination is ordered
next. A CBC and serum iron and ferritin should be done because, even
though the initial cause of vaginal bleeding may be dysfunctional bleeding,
the continued blood loss leads to iron deficiency anemia which may
perpetuate the bleeding. For the same reason, a thyroxine (T4) and TSH
should be ordered. An ANA, coagulation profile, and serum protein
electrophoresis may be useful to rule out other systemic causes, but at this
point of time a gynecologist should have been consulted.

635

 636

 VAGINAL DISCHARGE
ASK THE FOLLOWING QUESTIONS:
1. Is it purulent? A purulent vaginal discharge suggests nonspecific
bacterial vaginitis and gonorrhea. In contrast, the discharge of
bacterial vaginitis is white and has a fishy odor.
2. Is it frothy and yellow? This type of discharge is very often because
of trichomoniasis vaginitis.
3. Is it cheesy and associated with itching? These findings suggest
candidiasis vaginitis.
4. Is it watery and bloodstained? This type of discharge suggests
carcinoma of the cervix or endometrium, polyps, hydatidiform mole,
and chronic cervicitis. If a frankly bloody discharge is noted, consult
the differential diagnosis discussed on page 337.
5. Is it offensive smelling? An offensive smelling discharge would
suggest foreign body in the vagina.
6. Is there inflammation of the cervix? The presence of cervical
inflammation would suggest chronic cervicitis and gonorrhea.
DIAGNOSTIC WORKUP
The most important test is microscopic examination of a saline and
potassium hydroxide preparation. This will diagnose most cases of
trichomoniasis and candidiasis. Gardnerella vaginalis can be diagnosed if
clue cells are found, and the pH of the discharge will be greater than 4.7. If
this is unrevealing, a Gram’s stain for gonorrhea and cultures for
trichomoniasis, candidiasis, chlamydia, G. vaginalis, and gonorrhea may
be done. Recently, DNA probe or rapid antigen testing of urine may be
used to diagnose gonorrhea or chlamydia. If the results of these tests are
negative, look for pinworms. A Pap smear should be done to rule out
malignancy. Polyps or inflamed areas of the cervix should be biopsied.
Colposcopy may help further differentiate a cervical lesion. A dilation and
curettage may be necessary to diagnose endometrial carcinoma and
hydatidiform mole. Occasionally, pelvic ultrasound and CT scan are
necessary. However, before ordering these expensive diagnostic tests, a
gynecologist should be consulted. Patients with documented evidence of
gonorrhea should have a VDRL test and HIV testing. A therapeutic trial of
tetracycline or metronidazole may be successful in bacterial vaginitis.
637

 638

 VARICOSE VEINS
Varicose veins are common in the lower extremities and are usually not a
sign of other disease. Varicose veins of the rectum are called hemorrhoids
and can be a sign of cirrhosis of the liver or portal vein obstruction from
other causes. Distention of the abdominal veins may be because of
cirrhosis of the liver, thrombosis of the inferior vena cava, or distention of
the abdomen because of a large tumor (e.g., ovarian cyst), ascites, or
massive hepatic or splenic enlargement. Varicose veins of the thorax and
upper extremities are seen in mediastinal malignancies (primary or
metastatic), thoracic aortic aneurysms, and chronic fibrous mediastinitis.
DIAGNOSTIC WORKUP
Obviously, a liver profile will be important. Chest x-ray and a flat plate of
the abdomen should be routine. When these fail to identify a lesion—and
even when they do identify a lesion—it is often necessary to get a CT scan
of the thorax or abdomen. Exploratory surgery may be necessary to
establish a tissue diagnosis, as biopsy may be dangerous.

Hofstede’s Cultural Dimensions - Power Distance

Title: Power Distance Comparison: Hong Kong & United Kingdom

- Definition of Power Distance

- Hong Kong team members may be more comfortable with a hierarchical structure and may not question authority as much.
- UK team members may prefer a flatter structure and expect more equal input in decision-making.

- Strategies for managing Power Distance differences
- Text: To address these differences, project managers should:
- Establish clear communication channels, emphasizing open and respectful dialogue regardless of hierarchy.
- Encourage active participation of all team members in decision-making to balance the influence of hierarchy.
- Acknowledge the cultural expectations of both sides and create an environment that encourages the exchange of ideas and perspectives.

Prompts
 
A Prompt is a short text phrase that the Midjourney Bot interprets to produce an image. The Midjourney Bot breaks down the words and phrases in a prompt into smaller pieces, called tokens, that can be compared to its training data and then used to generate an image. A well-crafted prompt can help make unique and exciting images.
Structure
 
Basic Prompts
A basic prompt can be as simple as a single word, phrase or emoji
 
 
Advanced Prompts
More advanced prompts can include one or more image URLs, multiple text phrases, and one or more parameters
 
 
Image Prompts
Image URLs can be added to a prompt to influence the style and content of the finished result. Image URLs always go at the front of a prompt.
 
 
Prompt Text
The text description of what image you want to generate. See below for prompting information and tips. Well-written prompts help generate amazing images.
 
Parameters
Parameters change how an image generates. Parameters can change aspect ratios, models, upscalers, and lots more. Parameters go at the end of the prompt.
 
 
Prompting Notes
Prompt Length
Prompts can be very simple. Single words (or even an emoji!) will produce an image. Very short prompts will rely heavily on Midjourney’s default style, so a more descriptive prompt is better for a unique look. However, super-long prompts aren’t always better. Concentrate on the main concepts you want to create.
 
 
 
Grammar
The Midjourney Bot does not understand grammar, sentence structure, or words like humans. Word choice also matters. More specific synonyms work better in many circumstances. Instead of big, try gigantic, enormous, or immense. Remove words when possible. Fewer words mean each word has a more powerful influence. Use commas, brackets, and hyphens to help organize your thoughts, but know the Midjourney Bot will not reliably interpret them. The Midjourney Bot does not consider capitalization.
 
 
 
 
Focus on What you Want
It is better to describe what you want instead of what you don’t want. If you ask for a party with “no cake,” your image will probably include a cake. If you want to ensure an object is not in the final image, try advance prompting using the --no parameter.
 
 
 
Think About What Details Matter
Anything left unsaid may suprise you. Be as specific or vague as you want, but anything you leave out will be randomized. Being vague is a great way to get variety, but you may not get the specific details you want.
 
Try to be clear about any context or details that are important to you. Think about:
 
Subject: person, animal, character, location, object, etc.
Medium: photo, painting, illustration, sculpture, doodle, tapestry, etc.
Environment: indoors, outdoors, on the moon, in Narnia, underwater, the Emerald City, etc.
Lighting: soft, ambient, overcast, neon, studio lights, etc
Color: vibrant, muted, bright, monochromatic, colorful, black and white, pastel, etc.
Mood: Sedate, calm, raucous, energetic, etc.
Composition: Portrait, headshot, closeup, birds-eye view, etc.
 
 
Use Collective Nouns
Plural words leave a lot to chance. Try specific numbers. "Three cats" is more specific than "cats." Collective nouns also work, “flock of birds” instead of "birds.”
 
 
Basic Parameters
Aspect Ratios
--aspect, or --ar Change the aspect ratio of a generation.
 
Chaos
--chaos <number 0–100> Change how varied the results will be. Higher values produce more unusual and unexpected generations.
 
No
--no Negative prompting, --no plants would try to remove plants from the image.
 
Quality
--quality <.25, .5, 1, or 2>, or --q <.25, .5, 1, or 2> How much rendering quality time you want to spend. The default value is 1. Higher values cost more and lower values cost less.
 
Seed
--seed <integer between 0–4294967295> The Midjourney bot uses a seed number to create a field of visual noise, like television static, as a starting point to generate the initial image grids. Seed numbers are generated randomly for each image but can be specified with the --seed or --sameseed parameter. Using the same seed number and prompt will produce similar ending images.
 
Stop
--stop <integer between 10–100> Use the --stop parameter to finish a Job partway through the process. Stopping a Job at an earlier percentage can create blurrier, less detailed results.
 
Stylize
--stylize <number>, or --s <number> parameter influences how strongly Midjourney's default aesthetic style is applied to Jobs.
 
Uplight
--uplight Use an alternative "light" upscaler when selecting the U buttons. The results are closer to the original grid image. The upscaled image is less detailed and smoother.
 
Upbeta
--upbeta Use an alternative beta upscaler when selecting the U buttons. The results are closer to the original grid image. The upscaled image has significantly fewer added details.

Image Weight
--iw Sets image prompt weight relative to text weight. The default value is --iw 0.25.
 
Sameseed
--sameseed Seed values create a single large random noise field applied across all images in the initial grid. When --sameseed is specified, all images in the initial grid use the same starting noise and will produce very similar generated images
